title: Integration tests: route experiment routing (determinism, split accuracy, fallback precedence, metrics attribution)
creator: Sahana Iyer
content:
Overview
This ticket adds end-to-end coverage for the Route-level Experiments routing path. The goal is to catch the failure modes we’ve already seen in staging/beta (variant skew when sticky key missing; fallback overriding experiment; missing attribution in streaming retries) before GA.

Scope
- Deterministic assignment: same request + same stickiness inputs => same variant across process restarts and across regions.
- Split accuracy: allocation roughly matches configured traffic splits within tolerance.
- Precedence: experiment selection must be applied before fallback policy evaluation (and must not be silently bypassed by fallback/canary).
- Metrics attribution: request context + OTel spans contain experiment_id + variant_id; aggregator/rollup tables include {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id} dimensions.

Test strategy (what we actually run in CI)
We split tests into two layers to keep runtime/cost manageable:

A) Router-level integration tests (fast, deterministic; runs on every PR)
- Boot policy engine + router in-process with an in-memory experiment config cache.
- Exercise evaluateRoute(route_id, request_context) for N synthetic requests.
- Assert invariants on variant distribution, determinism, and evaluation order.

B) End-to-end smoke tests in ephemeral env (slower; runs on merge to main + nightly)
- Deploy minimal stack: experiment service + policy engine + router + OTel collector + metrics ingestion stub.
- Configure an experiment via the public-ish control plane API (same Console backend endpoints used by UI) and send real HTTP requests through gateway.
- Assert response headers + debug endpoint output + trace tags.

Test matrix
1) Determinism / stickiness key precedence
- Inputs tested:
  - explicit sticky_key (SDK option) present
  - customer_id present
  - session_id present
  - none present (expect: safe default path + warning + constrained behavior)
- Expectations:
  - When sticky_key present: assignment stable and independent of other IDs.
  - When sticky_key missing but customer_id present: stable on customer_id.
  - When no identifiers present: must not default to low-entropy key; assignment should fall back to per-request random bucket (non-sticky) OR “control-only” depending on config flag. Current expected behavior for GA: allow non-sticky assignment but emit attribution + warning; Console UI should show a validation warning and recommend configuring stickiness. (See ENG-28705 fix.)
- Implementation: In router integration tests we run 10,000 evaluations twice with a forced “restart” (reinitialize router + cache) and assert identical variant for each synthetic user.

2) Split accuracy
- Configs covered:
  - A/B 50/50
  - A/B 90/10
  - A/B/C 34/33/33
  - Edge: tiny split 99/1 (still should assign some traffic; guard against rounding-to-zero bugs)
- Method:
  - Generate 100k synthetic stable stickiness keys (UUIDv4) for each config.
  - Evaluate assignment and compute proportions.
- Acceptance criteria:
  - For each variant i, |observed_i - expected_i| <= max(0.5%, 5 * sqrt(p*(1-p)/N)).
  - Also assert no variant receives exactly 0 assignments unless expected split is 0.

3) Precedence & interactions (experiment vs fallback vs canary)
We’ve had regressions where fallback policy evaluation happened first, resulting in the experiment never being applied.

Expected evaluation order (validated by tests)
- Order in data plane routing:
  1) Normalize route_id (templated route, not raw path) for consistent bucketing + metrics.
  2) Evaluate experiment eligibility and deterministic assignment; select variant policy.
  3) Apply canary rollout policy (within the selected variant’s target policy/model set).
  4) Only then apply fallback (region/capacity/model variant fallback) if the chosen target is unavailable.

Scenarios covered:
- Experiment + fallback enabled, primary target unhealthy:
  - Expect: assignment picks a variant, then fallback triggers within that variant’s policy.
  - Assert: experiment attribution preserved even when fallback occurs.
- Route under canary rollout + experiment enabled:
  - Expect: experiment assignment first, then canary decision. (Canary remains about model version selection; experiment is about variant selection.)
  - Assert: canary does not “wash out” experiment attribution.
- Overlapping experiment config should be blocked by control plane validation (covered elsewhere); here we assert router behavior is deterministic given a single active experiment.

4) Metrics attribution (request context + OTel tags)
- For non-streaming request:
  - Assert response headers include:
    - x-redwood-experiment-id
    - x-redwood-experiment-variant
    - x-redwood-route-id (normalized)
  - Assert trace/span attributes include:
    - redwood.experiment_id
    - redwood.experiment_variant_id
    - redwood.route_id
- For streaming request + retry path:
  - Force a retry by injecting a synthetic mid-stream failure in the upstream model stub.
  - Assert attribution persists across the retry span and final response.
  - This specifically covers the regression fixed in PR-28622.

Test harness notes
- Repo location: redwood/tests/route_experiments/
- Main entrypoints:
  - TestDeterministicBucketing_* (router integration)
  - TestSplitAccuracy_* (router integration)
  - TestExperimentPrecedence_* (router integration)
  - TestE2EAttribution_* (ephemeral env)
- Determinism: all tests set a fixed hash salt in config; we explicitly assert that salt changes result in expected assignment churn (guardrail against accidental salt drift).
- Runtime: router integration suite ~2–3 minutes; e2e smoke ~8–12 minutes (runs nightly + post-merge).

Acceptance criteria
- CI gates:
  - Router integration suite must pass on PR.
  - Nightly e2e smoke must pass for 7 consecutive days prior to beta expansion.
- Coverage:
  - At least one test covering: determinism across restart, 90/10 split, fallback precedence, streaming retry attribution.
- Signal quality:
  - When failures occur, output must include the assignment debug explanation (hash inputs + selected variant + config version) to reduce oncall time.

Links / related work
- ADR-047 Deterministic experiment bucketing
- ADR-048 Experiment metrics attribution schema
- PR-28433 policy engine bucketing evaluator
- PR-28457 apply experiment selection before fallback
- PR-28622 fix attribution missing on streaming retries
- PR-28610 split accuracy tests (initial draft)

Results
- Added router integration tests for all core invariants.
- Added nightly e2e attribution smoke (streaming + retry path).
- Found + fixed one additional issue during implementation: route_id normalization mismatch between router and telemetry tags (fixed in follow-up PR; see comments).

Follow-ups (not in this ticket)
- Add a dedicated test for config propagation staleness bounds (ties to SLO doc; likely belongs in ENG-9023/ENG-9033).
- Consider adding a “cardinality budget” regression test for metrics tags (to catch accidental dimension explosion; see PR-28741).
comments: 2025-02-20 (Leila Farouk): Started harness work. Plan is two-tier: fast in-process router tests on every PR + nightly ephemeral env smoke for attribution/streaming. Will keep N=100k for split accuracy to get tight tolerance without flaking.

2025-02-27 (Jordan Lee): Confirmed expected stickiness precedence: explicit sticky_key > customer_id > session_id. If none present, we should avoid low-entropy defaults; either non-sticky per-request bucketing or control-only depending on config. Please ensure tests lock this in (we’ve seen skew from defaulting to IP hash).
2025-03-04 (Leila Farouk): Implemented determinism + split tests. Added restart simulation (re-init router + cache). Split tolerance set to max(0.5%, 5*sigma). All green locally.

2025-03-08 (Vikram Singh): Precedence test added for experiment-before-fallback. Also add a scenario where fallback occurs and we still preserve experiment attribution; this was part of the beta incident triage.

2025-03-12 (Caleb Johnson): For attribution assertions, please check both response headers and span attrs. OTel naming convention is redwood.experiment_id / redwood.experiment_variant_id per thread 1737750121.

2025-03-17 (Leila Farouk): Built initial e2e smoke for streaming + forced retry. Caught route_id normalization mismatch (router was tagging raw path in one codepath). Filed follow-up and patched; tests now assert normalized route template.

2025-03-22 (Sean Gallagher): Reviewed for GA gate. Request: on failure, dump assignment debug explanation (hash inputs + config version) to test logs so oncall can quickly see whether it’s skew vs propagation vs missing headers. Approved once added.
2025-03-28 (Leila Farouk): Added debug dump on assertion failure. Nightly e2e has been stable for the last week; marking Done.
